lesson_intro: Today is your first Revision Day. In the UPSC journey, studying is 40% of the work, but revising is 60%. If you don't consolidate what you learned in the last 6 days, you will lose the 'Article Number' and 'Schedule Number' precision that Prelims demands. Today is not for new topics. It is for active recall. Can you list all 12 Schedules without looking? Can you recall what Art 21, 25, or 32 specifically says? Use this day to fill the gaps in your memory. We have combined the most high-yield tables from the last 6 days into one master screen.

lesson_pages.intro: This block revises the constitutional foundations from Days 1–6. By the end you should be able to recall the 12 Schedules, the Fundamental Rights article map (12–35), the sources of the Constitution, and the Preamble & citizenship rules.
lesson_pages.title: UPSC REVISION: Block 1 (Days 1–6)

lesson_pages.intro: Schedules are tested by number and subject. The 7th Schedule matters most — it holds the Union, State and Concurrent Lists.
lesson_pages.title: The 12 Schedules — Quick Revision

blocks.text: 1: States & Union Territories, 2: Salaries & allowances — President · Governors · Speakers · Judges · CAG, 3: Forms of Oaths & Affirmations, 4: Allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to states & UTs, 5: Administration of Scheduled Areas & Scheduled Tribes, 6: Tribal Areas in Assam · Meghalaya · Tripura · Mizoram, 7: Union · State & Concurrent Lists (division of powers), 8: 22 Official Languages, 9: Laws protected from judicial review (1st Amendment 1951), 10: Anti-defection provisions (52nd Amendment 1985), 11: Panchayats — 29 subjects (73rd Amendment 1992), 12: Municipalities — 18 subjects (74th Amendment 1992)
